title: The Quiet Student Who Kept Moving Schools
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When Budi first joined my class, he barely spoke, and he never once raised his hand, even when he clearly knew the answer.
Narrator: [reflective] I later learned he had switched schools three times in two years, because his family moved constantly for his father's work.
Narrator: [gently] Each new school meant new rules, new classmates, and new gaps in what he had already learned before.
Narrator: [honestly] His grades reflected that instability, not a lack of intelligence, although some teachers before me had assumed otherwise.
Narrator: [warmly] I decided to give him small, private questions instead of calling on him in front of the whole class.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Slowly, he started answering correctly, quietly at first, then with a little more confidence each week that passed.
Narrator: [reflective] One afternoon, he stayed after class and admitted he thought he was simply bad at learning, like it was permanent.
Narrator: [gently] I told him that moving schools constantly would confuse anyone, and that his struggle made complete sense given his situation.
Narrator: [warmly] Something shifted in him after that conversation, as if permission to not be perfect finally allowed him to try harder.
Narrator: [with feeling] By the end of the semester, Budi was raising his hand regularly, and he even helped a classmate with a math problem.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I still remember his face when he received his first genuinely good grade, surprised, like he didn't fully trust the number on the page.
Narrator: [reflective] Teaching him taught me something important too, that struggling students often carry stories we never bother to ask about.
Narrator: [peacefully] Budi moved again the following year, unfortunately, but he wrote me a short letter before he left.
Narrator: [warmly] He said I was the first teacher who made him feel capable instead of behind, and I still keep that letter in my desk.
Narrator: [gently] Whenever a new quiet student joins my class now, I remember him, and I ask questions before I assume anything about their abilities.
